primary_topics: Keynote address at the Joint 18th Annual Convention of the Philippine Society of Hypertension and the Philippine Lipid and Atherosclerosis Society, February 13, 2013 -- structured around three 'orders' from Dr. Dante Morales (CJP's family physician): (1) crack a joke, (2) discuss a recent SC decision involving physicians, (3) say something inspirational

Order 1 -- The arthritis joke: a drunkard asks a priest at the Luneta what causes arthritis; after the priest delivers a stern moral lecture, the man reveals the Pope has arthritis. Moral: 'When sick, consult only doctors of medicine, not doctors of theology'

Order 2 -- Dr. Genevieve Huang v. Philippine Hoteliers (Dec 5, 2012): the gap between actual fact and legal fact -- a hard object fell on Dr. Huang's head at the Dusit Thani Hotel pool; the SC upheld the dismissal because the causal link between the hotel's negligence and her head injuries could not be legally proven to the required standard
Order 3 -- The good-news-bad-news parable applied to CJP's life: the farmer + CJP's own biographical arc including the specific mention of Boston University among his children's graduate schools
sub_topics: The doctor-as-authority framing: CJP generally refuses speeches since retirement; but 'I dare not disobey the order of our esteemed family friend and physician, Dr. Morales; an order which in law is equivalent to a subpoena'; Takusa Club -- 'Taking Court sa Asawa'; justices are courageous (sentence murderers; reverse the President) but afraid of only two: doctors and wives; here, both Leni AND Dr. Morales ordered CJP to accept

The arthritis joke: drunkard at Luneta asks a priest what causes arthritis; priest: 'loose living, being with cheap, wicked women, too much alcohol and sleeping with prostitutes'; drunkard: 'I just read here in the Inquirer that the Pope has arthritis'; moral: 'consult only doctors of medicine, not doctors of theology'

Dr. Huang v. Philippine Hoteliers (Dec 5, 2012): Dr. Huang and friend Delia Goldberg swam at Dusit Thani Hotel pool on June 11, 1995; after pool closed, a hard heavy folding wooden counter top fell on Dr. Huang's head; she experienced headaches and dizziness; various head injuries diagnosed; RTC ruled against her (no proof of direct and immediate result of accident); CA affirmed; SC upheld in 41-page decision -- 'Dr. Huang and her lawyers failed to prove the cause and effect connection between the fault or negligence of the hotel and the damages incurred by her'

Actual fact vs. legal fact: 'an event may have happened in truth and in reality. But if it cannot be proven in court according to the rules of evidence, it cannot be given credence in a judicial proceeding' -- the governing lesson for the physician audience

stances.claim: The Huang v. Philippine Hoteliers case illustrates the critical gap between actual fact and legal fact: an event may have genuinely occurred but if the cause-and-effect connection cannot be proven under the rules of evidence, the court cannot give it legal credence. This is the most important lesson for the physician audience -- medical certainty does not equal legal proof.
stances.rhetorical_move: actual-fact-vs-legal-fact lesson: the Huang case as a pedagogical example for physicians about why medical evidence may be insufficient for legal liability
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing lesson from the case

stances.claim: Even the Supreme Court Chief Justice is subject to the Takusa Club (Takot sa Asawa) -- justices are brave enough to sentence murderers and reverse the President, but afraid of two kinds of people: doctors and wives. Here both orders converge and become irresistible. This is the governing comedic framing for the entire speech.
stances.rhetorical_move: Takusa Club framing: the comedy of judicial courage deflated by domestic and medical authority as the self-deprecating opener

notable_anecdotes: The Takusa Club: 'Supreme Court Justices, including Chief Justices, are all members of the Takusa Club, meaning Takot sa Asawa. Justices are known to be courageous and sagacious; they sentence and imprison murderers, robbers, kidnappers and swindlers; they reverse and nullify actions of the President and Congress. They are not afraid of anyone, except only two sets of people: their doctors and their wives.' Here, both Dr. Morales AND Leni are aligned, making it 'not even appealable.'

The arthritis Pope joke: a drunkard at the Luneta asks a priest what causes arthritis; priest delivers a stern lecture about 'loose living, cheap wicked women, too much alcohol and sleeping with prostitutes'; drunkard: 'I just read here in the Inquirer that the Pope has arthritis.' Moral: 'When sick, consult only doctors of medicine, not doctors of theology.'

Dr. Huang's counter top: a 'hard and heavy object, which turned out to be a folding wooden counter top, fell on Dr. Huang's head' after the Dusit Thani pool closed -- the SC upheld the dismissal because despite the injury being real, the causal chain between the hotel's negligence and her specific head injuries could not be legally proven.

Boston University addition: in this version of the five-children arc, CJP says they finished graduate studies in 'Harvard, Stanford, University of California, University of Chicago, University of Michigan and Boston University' -- adding Boston University to the standard list.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered February 13, 2013 as the keynote address at the Joint 18th Annual Convention of the Philippine Society of Hypertension and the Philippine Lipid and Atherosclerosis Society, this address by CJP is structured around three 'orders' from his family physician Dr. Dante Morales -- who, CJP notes, has issued a subpoena equivalent that neither he nor even Leni can appeal: 'Supreme Court Justices are all members of the Takusa Club, meaning Takot sa Asawa. They are afraid of only two sets of people: their doctors and their wives.' Order 1 (crack a joke): a drunkard at the Luneta asks a priest what causes arthritis; the priest lectures about 'loose living, cheap wicked women, too much alcohol'; the drunkard: 'I just read here in the Inquirer that the Pope has arthritis.' Moral: 'When sick, consult only doctors of medicine, not doctors of theology.' Order 2 (recent SC decision involving physicians): Dr. Genevieve L. Huang v. Philippine Hoteliers (Dec 5, 2012) -- a heavy folding wooden counter top fell on Dr. Huang's head at the Dusit Thani Hotel pool after it closed; despite experiencing headaches and dizziness and being diagnosed with head injuries, the SC upheld the dismissal in a 41-page decision because she and her lawyers 'failed to prove the cause and effect connection between the fault or negligence of the hotel and the damages incurred by her.' CJP's pedagogical lesson: 'an event may have happened in truth and in reality. But if it cannot be proven in court according to the rules of evidence, it cannot be given credence in a judicial proceeding' -- the gap between actual fact and legal fact. Order 3 (something inspirational): the full good-news-bad-news parable (farmer with horse, ten wild horses, lame son, spared from war) applied to CJP's life -- the Yale denial becoming Baron Travel, whose revenues funded five children's graduate degrees at Harvard, Stanford, UC, Chicago, Michigan and Boston University.
